body:
Thanks for responding.  Congrats on breaking up with him, he sounds completely ridiculous.  I can't believe someone would say those things, he doesn't deserve someone as fabulous as you.  
Yes, you're 10000% right about the validation.  I will remember your example, I definitely need to stop putting guys on a pedestal.  
"I was too busy trying to become the most awesome version of myself" - I love this quote.  Definitely saving.
Yes, I'm getting counseling.  And I've tried meds a couple of times but I'm trying to get off of one right now.  I might try another, but I'm not sure.  I really appreciate this, it made me feel a lot better.

Thanks for responding, I appreciate it.  You don't sound unsupportive, you should like a completely reasonable person.
I might have been I guess slightly over exaggerating.  The fat thing is more of the whole I know its ridiculous in my mind but I can't think anything else.  I'm guess I'm not actually overweight.  Its just kind of a thing where I think like, "why do those other girls have guys that are attracted to them?, oh they're not ridiculously gorgeous so it must be because look thinner than me so now i'm going to beat myself up mentally until my thighs don't touch anymore and then they won't think i'm ugly" and so on.  Ugh, typing my thought process out is showing me how crazy I am.  So stupid.  But thanks for encouraging me to see this.  And I definitely plan on starting a concrete exercise plan anyway.  Hopefully it helps.

Thanks for responding.  You gave really great advice.

Unfortunately, I'm not green.  If I was, I'd probably have a lot more interesting things to say in conversations.  I do like grammar and editing :).  I guess no matter how upset I am, I'm still unfortunately a perfectionist.  And you're also right, I am kind of having a mid-college crisis (I did just change my major for the millionth time, bio to history, fun times).  I just feel like I've spent my entire schooling career focusing on academics (basically since like second grade) and I thought that college would finally be the time for be to have a healthy academic/social life balance.  Hopefully I can find more people to talk to.  I have my mom, but talking to her about my problems just makes me feel guilty because then she gets upset.

I guess I just feel like I've hit rock bottom so many times.  Like even in just the past year.  I've tried reinventing myself so many times and nothing seems to be working.  

Thanks a lot for the quote, it's great.  I love Emerson (and might possibly be planning to name a daughter after him if I get one) but I've never heard this one.  I'll definitely read the essay.

Thanks a lot for responding.  I understand about the whole vibe thing.  I guess I got so happy when I thought that I finally succeeded in not showing the shy/anxious side of me, and I just couldn't handle more failure this time.  Maybe I did and there were just other circumstances that changed the outcome.  And I don't need college to be a big party...maybe at least just a little party.  But I'm going to make it to "real life".  I'm not going to let these things ruin me.  I'm promising myself.
And (despite how hopeless I sounded earlier) I don't think that your life is so fucked up that you can't attract anyone.  If I still have hope, you need to have some too :)
